title: Jackson v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC found Jackson’s complaint administratively out of order and dismissed it for incurable lack of standing. Separately, it accepted jurisdiction over Presbytery’s failure to respond to his credible BCO 40-5 report and remitted the matter to Presbytery with instructions to address his concerns constitutionally.
first_summary: Jackson challenged Northwest Georgia Presbytery’s failure to act on his BCO 40-5 letter alleging delinquency by Midway’s Session. The SJC dismissed his complaint because he was not a commissioner at Presbytery’s January 2013 meeting. It nevertheless treated his correspondence as a credible report, accepted jurisdiction, and returned the matter to Presbytery for constitutional disposition.
summary: Jackson challenged Northwest Georgia Presbytery’s failure to act on his BCO 40-5 letter alleging delinquency by Midway’s Session. The SJC found his complaint administratively out of order and dismissed it because he was not a commissioner at Presbytery’s January 2013 meeting; originating a BCO 40-5 report did not confer standing. Separately, the SJC accepted jurisdiction over Presbytery’s failure to respond and remitted the matter for constitutional disposition, without deciding whether the Session committed the alleged delinquencies.

sources.supports: Case identity, adopted judgment, standing ruling, dismissal, BCO 40-5 action, remittal, and concurring qualifications.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The caption and decision identify Case 2013-08 and the SJC (printed p. 568, lines 13–20); the substitute decision was adopted 17–0 (printed p. 569, lines 50–54).
evidence_notes.dispute: The correspondence alleged important delinquency by Midway’s Session, and Presbytery failed to respond (printed p. 568, lines 29–46). The concurrence describes the underlying minutes and nominee issues (printed pp. 569–570, lines 60–71).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The complaint was administratively out of order and dismissed because Jackson lacked standing and a report’s source gains no standing merely from that role (printed p. 568, lines 19–27). The SJC accepted jurisdiction and remitted the matter to Presbytery (lines 29–46).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The separate concurrence states that the SJC did not find the Session delinquent; Presbytery must examine the allegations (printed p. 570, lines 71–73). Its further concerns about a possible BCO 40-5 loophole were not adopted reasoning (printed p. 571, lines 95–113).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No outside decision was incorporated by reference. The adopted ruling replaced a proposed panel decision that is not reproduced (printed p. 569, line 50).

source_limits: The source supplies the adopted decision and a separate concurrence but not the superseded proposed panel decision. The concurrence’s additional reasoning is not attributed to the SJC majority.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies Presbytery’s failure to act on the BCO 40-5 correspondence.
score_reasons.decision: States the administrative ruling, dismissal, accepted jurisdiction, and remittal.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains the standing defect and why originating the report did not cure it.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinction between standing to complain and supplying a credible BCO 40-5 report.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the adopted judgment from the concurrence and avoids finding the Session delinquent.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to explain the mixed procedural result and relief.

verification_notes: Rechecked the operative judgment at lines 19–46. The final summary adds the administrative subtype, the rule that report authorship did not confer standing, and the limitation that no underlying Sessional delinquency was decided.
